reason: The one-shot approval service with closed outcomes, the session policy and the asked and decided audit pair is kept; the answerer waterfall becomes ownership through the interaction registry, the decided record names who answered, and session grants are added.
A preset stays a named pair of sandbox mode and approval policy with a derived custom label; the table becomes live configuration and a switch is an owner action that revokes session grants.

Blocking and timed questions, late answers as user messages and the derived question projection are kept; delivery moves to the interaction registry, the claim stream becomes a host-owned deadline with a hold, and the approval intent is removed.
The model-facing ask_user_question tool is kept under the same name as one tool declaration with an optional timeout, replacing the two schemas selected by configuration.
The registry of human commands, global and agent-scoped registration and the logged run and done pair are kept; commands gain typed arguments and one dispatch entry that every carrier can call.

References and owner-scoped records, per-operation resolution and a describing call that never returns a value are kept as the secret contract; a redacting value type, leases with a revocation signal and enumeration of references are added.

The managed store over the launch environment and two .env files, with the stored value winning, is kept; the hand-editable YAML file becomes one machine-written file encrypted under a key held in the operating-system keychain, with an owner-only key file as the reported fallback.

Flows keyed by the record they write, one attempt per key and success only after an observed commit are kept; prompts become interaction registry items addressed to the starting peer and a flow can declare revocation.

System-browser sign-in with state and PKCE, authoritative local cancel, origin-bound release of request headers and local-first sign-out are kept; desktop embedding is dropped with the desktop application and notification polling becomes an opt-in setting.

Choosing the credential kind for one vendor request and releasing ready headers becomes the Authorizer interface of the account package; the presence-ordered auto billing is not carried because it changes who is billed without a record.

One random identifier per harness home is kept, but it is created only at the first use by a sender the user opted in to, stored in a key-value namespace in one transaction, and can be reset for every process at once.

The session remark event, the category list and the /feedback command are folded into the one feedback component together with message ratings; recording no longer prints or creates the anonymous identifier.
Ratings and notes on assistant messages as log-only events with per-item versions are kept; current items come from a registered projection instead of a scan and every event records the actor.

The vendor protocol still issues tokens with no expiry or refresh and accepts a loopback callback only, and a logout that keeps failing is retried in memory and not after a restart; the Go design keeps these because they are properties of the vendor service and of not storing a revoked token.
justification: The redirect addresses and token lifetime are decided by the vendor, not by the client, and persisting pending revocations would mean keeping the old token on disk. DH-ADR-HUMAN-11 and DH-ADR-HUMAN-10 state the limit and the user is told when issuer revocation failed.

reason: A request names its route and the authoriser reads that route's own endpoint and credential reference from configuration, so any number of key-authenticated vendor routes can exist; there is no single connection per kind.
The kind of a conversation's route is read from configuration and from the credential reference name in the logged request header, so it does not depend on which component is loaded at that moment.
Describe still reports presence only, so a wrong key counts as configured until the provider rejects it; checking a key needs a network call, which this area does not make unasked.
justification: A validity check is a request to the provider. Making it in the background would send traffic the user did not start; a user-started test call belongs to the model area and is listed as a request to area A04.

reason: A sign-in prompt is an interaction registry item addressed to the peer that started the attempt, so a browser reload receives the pending prompt again; only a host restart still abandons an attempt.
A flow may declare a Revoke operation; sign-out deletes the local record, closes its leases and then calls the issuer with bounded retries.
The authorisation service joins stored records with registered flows and lists each record as claimed or orphan, so the caller no longer has to recognise a record left by a removed component.
Describe returns a revision and Set takes the revision the caller saw, so a second writer of the same reference is refused instead of silently winning.

The keychain provider upstream deferred is built: stored values are encrypted under a key in the operating-system keychain and the secret directory is masked from confined commands where the sandbox backend can; the residual, an unconfined process of the same user asking the keychain, is stated in the security model.
The launch environment is still a snapshot taken at start, so a variable exported later in the launching shell is not seen; edits to the two .env files are watched and do apply.
justification: A running process cannot observe a later export in its parent shell on any operating system; this is not a property of the upstream runtime. The fallback layers that can change, the .env files, are watched by DH-D-HUMAN-7.

reason: A store write is a temporary file, a sync, a rename and a directory sync under a cross-process lock, so an acknowledged write survives a crash and an interrupted one leaves the old file whole.
The store has a References operation that returns every reference named by configuration or stored; the process starter needs it to scrub child environments and the settings form uses it.
A reference is still an environment-variable-shaped name in one flat namespace, because the environment and .env layers resolve it by that name; records keep the richer owner and id addressing.
justification: The environment fallback is a kept product rule (stored value first, then the launch environment), and it only works if the reference is a name the environment can hold. A credential that needs structure is a record.

reason: No notification can be raised for a variable changed in the launching shell, so a page that shows an environment-sourced credential learns of a change only after a restart.
justification: The cause is operating-system process semantics, the same as for the launch snapshot; changes to stored values and to the .env files do raise secret.ReferenceChanged, including for another process on the same home.

reason: The authorisation service, which holds the flow registry, reports for each record whether a registered flow claims it, so an orphan is identified by the service and can be deleted from the settings page.
The feedback service lists a session's current remarks and ratings from a projection for the UI and the SDK; no model-facing tool is added because feedback is not model context.
An entry gains an optional referenced event position, but it still carries one category and one text and has no severity field.
justification: No consumer in the design ranks feedback, so a severity field would be data nobody reads; it can be added to the event payload under a new payload version when a consumer exists.

reason: Recording feedback on a session with no live agent takes the session lease for the append, so a closed session accepts feedback; the case where another process holds the lease is the separate carried limit of message-feedback.3.
Each remark has an id and a feedback/withdrawn event removes it from the current view; history stays in the append-only log and deleting the session is the erasure operation.
The acknowledgement is returned only after the append was flushed, so an acknowledged entry survives a crash.
The acknowledgement is a server-rendered fragment of the feedback form and does not depend on the transcript having rows, so a blank session shows it too.
Command dispatch is one service call that the browser, the command line and the SDK all reach, so /feedback is available wherever a carrier exists.
The message_feedback sidecar is an earlier upstream storage format; the Go design reads no upstream format and never had a sidecar, so there is nothing to migrate (DH-ADR-2).
Deleting a rating or withdrawing a remark removes the current item only; earlier values stay in the append-only session log.
justification: The append-only log is the single source of truth (DH-ADR-PERSISTENCE-1) and committed events are immutable; erasure is deleting the session, which the session store area provides.

reason: When another dsh process holds a session's write lease, a feedback change made here is refused with an error that names the busy session; the request is not forwarded to that process.
justification: A session has exactly one writer, the lease holder (DH-ADR-12, DH-ADR-PERSISTENCE-4), and the design has no channel between hosts on one home; the session store area lists cross-process delivery as open.

reason: Every feedback event records the actor (principal, channel and peer) taken from the admitted connection, and a non-owner needs a role on the session to write feedback.

Recording feedback sends nothing; a session is uploaded only when the user turned the setting on and confirmed a preview of the redacted records for that submission, and a baseline redactor always runs.
Current feedback is a registered projection whose checkpoint commits with its events, so list, put and delete read state without scanning the session log.
The feedback component caps the number of feedback events per session as well as the size of one note and one text, and refuses further changes with a limit error.
Resetting or losing the identifier creates a new anonymous identity that cannot be linked to the old one.
justification: This is the anonymity property itself: recovery would need stable material derived from the machine or the user, which the design refuses. DH-ADR-HUMAN-12 states it as intended behaviour.

reason: The identifier is created by one insert-if-absent transaction in the shared database, so two processes that race get the same value and no run uses a private one.
Two harness homes have unrelated identifiers and cannot be correlated.
justification: Linking homes would need an identifier outside the home, which is a machine or user identifier; the design keeps the identifier home-scoped on purpose (DH-ADR-HUMAN-12).

reason: The identifier is attached to a model request only when that route's Installation switch is on, and Ensure refuses to create or return it for a purpose the user did not enable, so a configured gateway receives nothing by default.
The identifier is read through the key-value store's revision check and not memoised per process, so a reset takes effect at once in every process on the home.
A command may declare a Go argument struct from which validation, the UI form, completion and the SDK schema are derived; raw text remains as one argument type among others.
A command handler must still honour cancellation; one that does not is settled as aborted after a grace period and tracked as detached, and its side effects are uncertain.
justification: Go cannot stop a goroutine, so cancellation of in-process code is cooperative by nature; the design bounds the wait and reports the detached handler instead of hiding it (DH-ADR-HUMAN-8).

reason: A permission preset still bundles two knobs, sandbox mode and approval policy, and does not choose the agent composition.
justification: Which tools and prompt an agent has is the agent preset of the bundle and preset area; folding it into the Permissions choice would make one control change both authority and capability. A network knob can be added once the sandbox area exposes a per-session setter.

reason: The preset table is live configuration that the settings form edits in the writable layer, so a user who wants a named combination adds an entry and selects it; custom stays the label for an unmatched pair.
The preset component accepts a configuration update in place and notifies preset.CatalogChanged, so the table can change without reloading the component.
The reserved auto preset still cannot be the default for new sessions.
justification: Auto is contributed by an experimental, default-off review component; a default that names an entry which may not be loaded would leave new sessions without a valid permission state.

reason: The default preset must still name an entry of the table, so removing that entry and changing the default happen in one configuration edit; an edit that breaks the rule is rejected with its position.
justification: Falling back to some other preset when the named default disappears would change a security default without the operator saying so; strict validation of the whole edit is the fail-closed choice.

reason: There is one tool schema, so every call is tracked by the questions projection and any call can return pending or take a late answer.
A nested call made through the tool command line is logged when it is admitted, before its body runs, so the projection can reconstruct the question even if the calling script ends first.
A child agent is unbound by default, so its question is refused and it must put the open question in its result; the registry offers a binding through the parent that the delegation area may turn on.
justification: A person who delegated work did not necessarily expect prompts from nested agents, and the rule for subagents belongs to the delegation area; this area supplies the mechanism (rule 5 of who may answer) and keeps the fail-closed default.

reason: The tool renders its answer for the model as one readable line per question through the declaration's render function, while the structured value stays in the log.
A request may be made outside a turn: the turn requirement existed to tell an audit event from a crash tail, which the transactional store does not have, and an open pair found on resume is closed.
Session grants add a standing yes for one directory or one application that is logged, listed and revocable and ends with the session; nothing is stored across sessions.
The request still references the call by id, and the interaction item resolves the tool's presentation of the logged arguments, so every answerer (browser, SDK, ACP) shows what is being approved.
Each interactive profile mounts the answerer of its carrier and binds the agents it creates; the headless profile mounts none on purpose, so the answer there is no by design and not by omission.
A pending approval is still not restored after a host restart; on resume the open audit pair is closed as unavailable and the call is denied.
justification: After a crash the interrupted turn is closed and never continued (design section 5), so there is no call left to approve; re-asking would approve an action the driver will not run. The closer keeps the log honest.

reason: An interaction's audience is an agent or a peer, so a caller without an agent (a sign-in prompt, a consent from a command) is routed to the peer that started it instead of needing a local listener.
A question is still selectable options plus optional text; file pickers and diff confirmations have no interaction kind.
justification: Interaction kinds are a closed set because each needs a payload type, a rendered fragment and a mapping in the SDK and ACP protocols; a new kind is added when a tool needs it, not speculatively.

reason: Unfinished answer text stays in the browser tab that holds it and is not stored by the host.
justification: A draft is not a decision; storing keystrokes of an unanswered question on the host would add a write path and a second copy to keep consistent across tabs for no effect on the outcome.

reason: A vendor business failure is reported with its numeric code and a message-catalogue entry keyed by that code, falling back to a generic message that shows the code; specific copy per code is still missing.
justification: The list of business codes and the wording for each are a vendor product decision that the pinned source does not contain; the catalogue key exists so copy can be added without a code change.

reason: The Go harness exposes the same tool name with one schema: questions as upstream plus an optional timeout in seconds where -1 waits; a timed call returns pending and a later answer arrives as a user message.
No waterfall event is dispatched: the approval service asks the interaction registry, which delivers the item to the one answerer bound to the agent, so listener order cannot decide who answers.
Replaced by the notify-form key authz.Settled carrying the record key and the outcome, sent after the key is released.
Replaced by the notify-form key command.Changed carrying the scope, sent after a registration or removal commits.
Replaced by the notify-form key secret.RecordChanged carrying the record key and the operation; a deletion also fires the revocation signal of every lease on that record.
Replaced by the notify-form key secret.ReferenceChanged carrying the reference name and whether the change was local or made by another process.
No event is needed: a model request on the account route without a sign-in settles as an attempt record with the code llm/sign-in-required, which the user interface already renders.
Replaced by the notify-form key account.Expired, sent after a 401 from the vendor cleared the local grant.
Replaced by the notify-form key account.SignedOut, sent after the local grant was removed and before its leases are closed.

The event existed so that an uploader could send the session when feedback was committed; recording now sends nothing and an upload starts only from the user's confirmed preview, so no hook is needed.
Replaced by the notify-form key preset.CatalogChanged, sent when the live preset table or the reserved auto entry changes.
No waterfall event is dispatched: the question service asks the interaction registry, which delivers the item to the answerer bound to the agent or to the peer that started the operation.
Replaced by the Go struct secret.Config: backend auto, keychain or file, the two .env layers, watch, debounce and lock wait; the store path is no longer configurable because the home layout fixes it.

Replaced by the Go struct account.Config with the three origins, timeouts and logout retries as upstream, header values as text or credential references and a notifications setting that is off by default; the desktop platform field is gone.
Replaced by the Go struct feedback.Config with a default note limit of 8192 bytes, a text limit and a cap on feedback events per session.
Replaced by the Go struct preset.Config holding the preset table and the default preset as live configuration, validated so that the default names an entry.
Replaced by the Go config of the tool.ask-user component with a default and a maximum timeout; the mode field is gone because there is one schema.
Replaced by the Go struct approval.Config: the default policy as upstream, plus a prompt timeout and the session-grant settings (allowed scope kinds and a per-session cap).
ctx.approval becomes approval.Service under approval.Key: Request, the session policy and the session-grant operations.
ctx.authorization becomes authz.Service under authz.Key: flow registration, one attempt per record, sign-out with revocation and the list of records with their claim state.
ctx.commands becomes command.Registry under command.Key: scoped registration, discovery and one Execute entry for every carrier.
ctx.credentials becomes secret.Store under secret.Key: leases for references, description without the value, one-way writes, records, enumeration and masking.
ctx.deepseekAccount becomes account.Service under account.Key: sign-in, sign-out, on-demand profile and balance, and host-only release of request headers.
ctx.deepseekAuth becomes the account.Authorizer interface under account.AuthKey in the account package; it returns ready headers for one kind and never tries a second.
ctx.messageFeedback is folded into feedback.Service under feedback.Key, which serves message ratings and session remarks from one projection.
ctx.permissionPresets becomes permission.Service under permission.Key: the catalogue, the current selection and the owner-only switch.
ctx.sessionFeedback is folded into feedback.Service under feedback.Key together with message ratings; it works on a closed session by taking the lease for the append.
ctx.userQuestions becomes question.Service under question.Key: ask with a deadline through the interaction registry, the hold, and Reply for a late answer.

Final verdict after reading the note: the closed four-outcome vocabulary, fail closed with no answerer, the never policy inside the service and the audit pair are kept, but the waterfall of answerer listeners is replaced by one registry with a binding per agent, because the note itself says sibling order is not deterministic and tells deployments to compose one terminal answerer.

Final verdict: the two settlements are kept (pending at the deadline, a later answer as a durable user message, never an approval); the client claim stream is replaced by a host-owned deadline with a hold tied to the view's connection, and the legacy and timed schemas become one.

Final verdict: the stored document belongs to the store alone and is never loaded into the process environment, and the gap against the model's own tools is stated plainly; the keychain the note records as the deferred real answer is built. The note's route-registration half belongs to the model area.

Final verdict: kept as written. A stored value wins over the launch environment and the two .env files for every provider, a save always takes effect, and Describe reports which layer supplied the value; a one-run override uses a separate harness home.

Final verdict: the second key space of owner-scoped records, flows that own the write and success only after an observed commit are kept. Two parts change: prompts become registry items addressed to the starting peer so a reload re-attaches, and a flow can declare revocation. The pi-ai translations named in the first verdict do not exist in Go.

Final verdict: system-browser sign-in, authoritative local cancellation, success only after the grant is stored and sign-out that removes the local grant first are kept. The Electron embedding and per-desktop client identity in the note are dropped with the desktop application.

Final verdict: one owner of the credential choice that hands out ready headers bound to an origin and a revocation signal is kept, inside the account package. The note's auto billing order, which takes the first kind that has a credential, is not carried: the Go authoriser uses the kind of the conversation's route or the configured default and never tries a second kind, so who is billed never changes silently.

Final verdict: feedback as log-only events in the canonical session log with per-item versions and fork isolation is kept. The note's delivery half, feedback riding on a default-on session-log contribution and an upload triggered by feedback, is replaced by an explicit, previewed and confirmed send with a local export alternative.

title: One interaction registry, four closed kinds, settled exactly once
Answerers register per channel; the creating carrier binds the agent; nothing transfers automatically
Approvals: five closed outcomes, policy before people, an attributed audit pair, no turn requirement
A session grant names a subject scope from a closed set and is matched on facts
A grant lives and dies with the one live session it was given to and is never copied
A preset bundles two knobs; switching is an owner action that is logged and revokes grants
One question tool with two settlements; a permission decision is never a question
Commands are typed host actions that any carrier can dispatch and the model never sees
Secrets: a redacting type, one store, a keychain-held key over an owner-only file, stored wins, never in the environment
A sign-in is an interaction addressed to whoever started it; sign-out is local first and then revokes
The vendor account: host-only release bound to an origin, no presence-ordered billing, no unasked vendor traffic
The anonymous identifier does not exist until the user opts in to something that sends it
Feedback is recorded locally; sending is a separate step that shows what will be sent; local export is always offered
A pending approval or question lives in one registry and only the bound channel can settle it
An approval returns one closed outcome and leaves an attributed audit pair
A user can grant one directory or one application for the session, see the grants and revoke them
One Permissions choice sets sandbox mode and approval policy together
The model can ask the user a question, wait or move on, and still get a late answer
A person runs a command against an agent from any client without a model turn
Configuration names a secret; the value sits behind one store and cannot be printed, logged or inherited
Stored secrets are encrypted under a key in the operating-system keychain, and a person can sign in and out
A user can sign in to the vendor account, and an installation has an identifier only after opting in
Feedback is saved locally, and nothing is sent until the user has seen exactly what will be
An interaction settles exactly once; late, cancelled and unloaded cases change nothing
Only the bound channel settles an agent's item; an unbound agent gets unavailable; one answerer per channel
Each approval outcome; never rejects before grants and answerers; a panic, a timeout or a failed append never allows
The decided record names the actor; a request outside a turn is accepted; an open pair is closed on resume
A grant covers a matching subject and no other, for directories and applications
Revocation, disposal and a policy switch end a grant; resume, fork and a child agent start with none; only an owner creates one
Preset pinning, switching, the custom label, owner-only switching and default validation
Blocking and timed questions, the hold, one late answer as a user message, nested calls in the projection
Command dispatch: unknown names, scoping, typed arguments, the logged pair, owner-only commands, a handler that ignores cancellation
The secret type prints redacted through every formatter, encoder, logger and template; parse errors carry no value
Layer precedence, revision check, two-process record updates, durable write, and no handler returns a value
No stored value or .env entry reaches a child environment or the process environment; released values are masked in tool results; unset fires the lease signal
Keychain envelope with a fake keychain: round trip, reported fallback, explicit mode fails closed, lost key, tampered file
Authorisation attempts: one per key, decline, commit confirmation, re-attach after reconnect, sign-out with revocation, orphan records
Account sign-in state and cancel checks, origin-bound release, no second credential kind, no vendor request on a fresh home
The anonymous identifier is absent on a fresh home, created only for an enabled purpose, single under a race, and reset for all processes
Feedback record, withdraw, rate, version conflict, list, actor, flush before acknowledgement, cap, fork isolation
Recording feedback never previews or authorises an upload; send needs confirmation; the export equals the preview
A real browser approves and rejects one call at a time
A real browser grants a directory for the session, lists it, revokes it, and finds nothing after a restart
With an SDK client and a browser connected, only the creator answers; with nobody, the answer is no
A stored key sits behind a real keychain and reaches neither a child process nor a confined read
Vendor sign-in through the system browser: cancel, reload, complete, sign out
The feedback form shows its payload before anything is sent, and offers export
A timed question returns pending, and its late answer becomes a user message after a restart
Operating-system keychain access (Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service) for the one data key of the secret store
verified: go list -m -json github.com/zalando/go-keyring@latest and the LICENSE file in the module cache, 2026-11-18; no file imports C; building with cgo off was not run
